# Autopsy of a Dead Project — submission README

Forensic pathology for software. Paste a GitHub repo, get a death certificate: cause of death, differential diagnosis, recovered last words, and an engine badge that never hides which model called it. If the repo is alive, you get a certificate of life instead.

Built for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4 (Ghost in the Machine). The full narrative write-up (the judged submission) is the DEV post:
https://dev.to/dmustapha/i-built-a-coroner-for-dead-software-it-issues-death-certificates-and-it-refuses-to-lie-2o07

## The problem
Every developer has a graveyard of repos that stopped and never restarted. There is no honest, defensible read on how they died, just a vibe. A classifier that stamps "cause of death" has to be trustworthy, which means it cannot be a black box.

## What it is
An open-weight prediction system. TabPFN (Prior Labs tabular foundation model, run locally) produces the verdict as a posterior over six death modes. An open-weight LLM (deepseek-v4.1-flash via 0G Compute) reads the evidence, breaks TabPFN's closest calls, and writes the eulogy. A grounding gate refuses any eulogy that does not trace to the real README/commit record.

## Our open-source AI integration
- TabPFN, local, the verdict: `app/classifier.py`
- deepseek-v4.1-flash on 0G Compute, narration + tie-break: `app/main.py`, `app/narrator.py`
- Held-out eval vs a 1-NN baseline: `scripts/eval_loo.py`
- Grounding gate + tests: `app/narrator.py`, `tests/test_narration_grounding.py`

## What makes it different
It knows the edge of what it knows. It shows the full posterior, proves its instrument beats a dumb baseline on a held-out test, recovers real last words instead of inventing them, and says "I could not ground that" rather than narrate a death it cannot defend.

## Verify in 60s
The headline claim is "the foundation model beats the dumb baseline on a held-out test." Re-derive it yourself, do not take the number on faith:

```
git clone https://github.com/dmustapha/autopsy-of-a-dead-project && cd autopsy-of-a-dead-project
pip install -r requirements.txt
python scripts/eval_loo.py
```
Expected: TabPFN leave-one-out ≈ 58.1%, 1-NN baseline ≈ 43.6% (a ~14.5 point gap) over the 117-repo corpus.
